contents.name: 5.3 / Theorem 5.3.1 (Gromov polynomial growth theorem)
contents.reason: The converse from polynomial growth to virtual nilpotence is substantially beyond proving growth of a given nilpotent group; it is not used in any proposed proof.

contents.name: Definition 5.3.2 (virtually nilpotent part)
contents.reason: This pair proves the formula for nilpotent groups themselves; finite-index extensions and Gromov rigidity are not prerequisite steps.

contents.name: Definition 5.3.3 (virtual solvability)
contents.reason: Virtual solvability and its growth alternatives are outside the specified nilpotent-coordinate proof route.

contents.name: Example 5.3.4: free groups and virtual solvability
contents.reason: Free-group virtual nonsolvability is not needed for any coordinate or growth estimate for nilpotent groups.

contents.name: Example 5.3.4: finite groups and virtual nilpotence
contents.reason: The distinction between virtual nilpotence and solvability is unrelated to the torsion reduction within a nilpotent group.

contents.name: Example 5.3.4: solvable semidirect-product example
contents.reason: Hyperbolic matrix semidirect products concern exponential growth of solvable groups and are not used in the nilpotent proof.

contents.name: Proposition 5.3.5 (central lower factors)
contents.support: Centrality is also established locally; finite generation requires the additional simple-commutator argument.

contents.name: 5.3.2 / Theorem 5.3.6
contents.support: Supports the degree statement, not its omitted general proof.

contents.reason: The last-term estimate is the exact estimate required here. General lower-central subgroup distortion is not used and must not be misidentified with pointwise degree equal to its layer.

contents.name: Proposition 14.25: weighted bounds
contents.support: The converse box inclusion is proved locally by quotient lifting plus central correction, using only earlier lemmas.

contents.support: Replace the appeal to growth invariance by exact fiber cardinality inequalities.

contents.name: Theorem 14.26: rank bookkeeping
contents.support: Prove the induced-factor finite-kernel statement explicitly.

contents.name: Proposition 14.22 (general subgroup polynomial distortion)
contents.reason: General subgroup distortion requires extension estimates unnecessary for the last central layer or the prescribed growth theorem.

contents.name: Lemma 14.23 (distortion in a diagram of extensions)
contents.reason: This supplier serves general subgroup distortion only, whereas our proof uses direct fibers of a central quotient.

contents.name: Theorem 14.24 (rational distortion exponents and Osin formula)
contents.reason: Classifying all subgroup distortion exponents goes beyond exact distortion of the last central term and is not invoked.
